items.title: Canonical KL through the explicit restricted-fiber log ratio

source.edition: arXiv:2010.03106v4, as cited by SPHMC arXiv:2609.06906v1
source.attribution: Lee--Shen--Tian and Chen--Chewi--Lu--Zhang supply the entropy/score route. The generic canonical-KL interface is ASTIS's rigorous supporting expansion; no author endorsement implied.

items.statement: For two normalized exponential tilts of one nonzero sigma-finite base, integrability of the explicit normalized log ratio under the left tilt makes the canonical KL finite and identifies its real value with the integral of that explicit representative. This isolates the measure-theoretic step used before differentiating the restricted-fiber score.
assumptions: The common base is nonzero and sigma-finite.
Both exponential weights are integrable, and the left exponent is measurable.
The displayed normalized log ratio is integrable under the left tilted probability law.

obligations.label: Convert the canonical finite KL to the explicit normalized log-ratio integral without transporting gradients

bindings.boundary: Finite-KL and exact explicit integral only. Restricted-fiber integrability, score differentiation, LSI, Fisher, T2 and W2 contraction remain separate.

assumption_deltas.source: The source entropy/score proof manipulates normalized restricted-Gaussian density ratios.
assumption_deltas.lean: A generic nonzero sigma-finite base, integrable exponential weights, measurable left exponent and explicit left-law L1 ratio.
assumption_deltas.reason: These hypotheses make normalization, absolute continuity, canonical llr integrability and the real KL integral formula valid.

assumption_deltas.source: The source differentiates a displayed smooth representative.
assumption_deltas.lean: This theorem uses a.e. equality only for integrability and integral congruence; it contains no derivative conclusion.
assumption_deltas.reason: Classical derivatives cannot be transported through arbitrary a.e. equality.
